Confirming on Desktop **1.17.9** (Windows 11) — and notably **not** just CLI/dev builds.

Every session created through the packaged Desktop app gets `version = 'local'`
and is therefore hidden from the sidebar after a restart, even though it persists
fine. No `opencode` CLI involved here.

Evidence:
- All sessions are present in `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` (`session`
  table, messages in `message`/`part`) — nothing is lost.
- `SELECT version FROM session` → every row is `'local'`.
- The Desktop even keeps per-session state in
  `%APPDATA%/ai.opencode.desktop/opencode.workspace.*.dat`
  (`workspace:model-selection` lists each session id), so the app clearly knows
  the sessions exist — only the sidebar list filters them out.
- Sessions were created via a custom OpenAI-compatible provider in
  `opencode.jsonc` (Ollama Cloud, direct `https://ollama.com/v1`).

So the version filter makes the sidebar appear empty on every restart for normal
end users of the Desktop build, not only `local`/dev sessions.

I found an interesting workaround: give each clone a distinct but GitHub-equivalent remote URL by varying the casing of your username/org name. For example, `https://github.com/janekhaertter/repo.git` and `https://github.com/JANEKHAERTTER/repo.git` resolve to the same repo on GitHub, but OpenCode treats them as different URLs.

This gives up to `2^n` distinct workspace URLs, where `n` is the number of alphabetic characters in the GitHub username/org name :)

I can also reproduce a related issue after downgrading the TUI from `1.17.10` to `1.17.9` as a workaround for the Bun crash on Windows.

After the downgrade, continuing existing sessions created or touched by `1.17.10` causes all subagent dispatches in the TUI to fail. The background subagents are no longer observable via the shortcut, and it is unclear whether they are actually running, blocked, or failed silently.

The TUI also reports the following SQLite error when trying to continue the previous conversation or dispatch subagents:

```text
SQLiteError: no such column: replacement_seq
```

This looks like a local SQLite schema incompatibility after `1.17.10` writes or migrates the session database, and then `1.17.9` tries to read it. So while downgrading to `1.17.9` avoids the Bun segmentation fault, it breaks existing sessions and subagent dispatch due to the database schema mismatch.

Environment:

* OS: Windows 11
* OpenCode TUI: downgraded from `1.17.10` to `1.17.9`
* Install method: Scoop
* Previous `1.17.10` crash: Bun `1.3.14`, Windows x64, standalone executable, segmentation fault

@nikitakot I’m seeing something similar. Downgrading from `1.17.10` to `1.17.9` avoids the Bun segfault, but it does not seem to be a clean rollback.

My guess is that `1.17.10` already migrated or partially updated the local SQLite project/session storage. After that, `1.17.9` still reads the same local DB but does not understand the newer schema, which leads to errors like:

```text
SQLiteError: no such column: replacement_seq
```

So even new sessions in `1.17.9` may fail if they are using the same already-migrated local storage. This probably requires either an official rollback migration or manually backing up and resetting the local OpenCode project/session data.

So the current behavior is:

* `1.17.9` new session + main model: works
* `1.17.9` new session + subagent dispatch: broken
* `1.17.10`-touched sessions continued in `1.17.9`: broken, even after fork/compact

Closing this — it's both ineffective and redundant.

**Redundant:** `dev` already reverted the OpenTUI 0.4.2 bump in #33842 (merged), so `@opentui/solid` is back to 0.3.4 (single-entry) where npm-spec TUI plugins load fine. The regression no longer exists on `dev`.

**Ineffective:** I verified the `nodeModulesBareSpecifiers: true` change in this PR does **not** actually fix the bug against the real 0.4.2 packaging. With the flag on, importing the plugin's `dist/tui.tsx` from `node_modules` still throws `Export named 'jsxDEV' not found ... jsx-runtime.d.ts`, and `host RendererContext === plugin RendererContext` is still `false`.

Root cause of why the flag is insufficient (for whoever re-attempts the 0.4.2 bump): the proximate failure is OpenTUI's Solid babel transform (`@opentui/solid/scripts/solid-plugin.js`), whose file filter hardcodes a `node_modules` exclusion:

```js
const sourceFilter = input.resolvePath
  ? /^(?!.*[/\\]node_modules[/\\]).*\.[cm]?[jt]sx?(?:[?#].*)?$/
  : /^(?!.*[/\\]node_modules[/\\]).*\.[cm]?[jt]sx(?:[?#].*)?$/;
```

npm-spec plugins live under `~/.cache/opencode/.../node_modules/`, so the Solid transform never runs on them, Bun falls back to native JSX, and `@jsxImportSource @opentui/solid` resolves `@opentui/solid/jsx-runtime` to the plugin's bundled stub. That exclusion is in a different Bun plugin and is not gated by `nodeModulesBareSpecifiers`. There's also a version-skew dimension (plugin bundles its own older `@opentui/solid`, distinct instance from the host). Details in #33884.

So: the revert is the correct fix for now. If 0.4.2 is re-attempted, the durable fix is to make npm-spec plugins resolve the host's `@opentui/*` (dedup/override at install) and/or relax the Solid transform's `node_modules` exclusion for the plugin cache tree — not this flag.

**Update: already addressed on `dev` by the OpenTUI 0.4.2 revert (#33842, merged).** `dev` is back on `@opentui/solid@0.3.4` (single-entry), which is the version where npm-spec TUI plugins load correctly. So this regression is fixed for the next release; it only affects the shipped **1.17.10** build. Workaround for 1.17.10 users remains: reference the plugin by an absolute `file://` path in `tui.json`.

Leaving this open as a guardrail for any **future re-attempt of the 0.4.2 bump**, because I verified the obvious one-line fix does **not** work and the real fix is non-trivial:

- Tried `ensureRuntimePluginSupport({ rewrite: { nodeModulesBareSpecifiers: true } })` (proposed in #33885). Result: plugin import still throws `Export named 'jsxDEV' not found ... jsx-runtime.d.ts`, and `host RendererContext === plugin RendererContext` is still `false`. That flag only affects the core runtime-plugin's bare-import rewriting; it does not touch the path that breaks.
- The proximate blocker is OpenTUI's Solid babel transform (`@opentui/solid/scripts/solid-plugin.js`), whose source filter hardcodes a `node_modules` exclusion (`(?!.*[/\\]node_modules[/\\])`). npm-spec plugins live under `~/.cache/opencode/.../node_modules/`, so the transform never runs on them → Bun native JSX → `@jsxImportSource @opentui/solid` resolves to the plugin's bundled `jsx-runtime.d.ts` stub (0.4.x ships a real `jsx-runtime.js`, but the plugin pinned its own older `@opentui/solid`).
- Confirmed by relocating the identical plugin code to a path outside `node_modules`: the `jsxDEV` throw disappears (advances to unrelated missing-dep errors). This is exactly why `file://` plugins work and npm-spec plugins don't.

Durable fix for a future 0.4.x bump (either/both):
1. Make npm-spec plugins resolve the host's `@opentui/*` instead of bundling their own — dedup/override `@opentui/*` (and `solid-js`) to the host versions during the Arborist install in `packages/core/src/npm.ts`. This fixes both the JSX-runtime stub and the duplicate-instance/version-skew.
2. Upstream: relax the Solid transform's `node_modules` exclusion so it still transforms files inside the opencode plugin cache tree.

#33885 (the `nodeModulesBareSpecifiers` PR) has been closed as ineffective + redundant.
